quotes.text: Stand in a split-stance position holding a dumbbell with both hands and wrap both hands around the dumbbell handle.
quotes.closest: Stand in a split-stance position holding a dumbbell with both hands and wrap both hands around the dumbbell handle.

quotes.text: Hold the weight overhead by grasping the inside dumbbell plate surface with both hands, or by grasping both handles of the kettlebell.
quotes.closest: Hold the weight overhead by grasping the inside dumbbell plate surface with both hands, or by grasping both handles of the kettlebell.

quotes.text: Stiffen your torso by contracting your abdominal/core muscles ("bracing"), and depress and retract your scapulae (pull your shoulders down and back), maintaining this position throughout the exercise.
quotes.closest: Stiffen your torso by contracting your abdominal/core muscles ("bracing"), and depress and retract your scapulae (pull your shoulders down and back), maintaining this position throughout the exercise.

quotes.text: Your head and neck should be aligned with your spine.
quotes.closest: Your head and neck should be aligned with your spine.

quotes.text: Exhale and slowly press the dumbbell overhead, extending your elbows until your arms are vertical to the floor, elbows pointing forward, but not completely locked.
quotes.closest: Exhale and slowly press the dumbbell overhead, extending your elbows until your arms are vertical to the floor, elbows pointing forward, but not completely locked.

quotes.text: The dumbbell should be positioned directly over your head with your palms facing upwards and the dumbbell hanging vertically or angled slightly.
quotes.closest: The dumbbell should be positioned directly over your head with your palms facing upwards and the dumbbell hanging vertically or angled slightly.

quotes.text: Inhale and allow the weight to slowly bend your elbows, lowering the dumbbell behind your head in a controlled manner without moving your upper arms.
quotes.closest: Inhale and allow the weight to slowly bend your elbows, lowering the dumbbell behind your head in a controlled manner without moving your upper arms.

quotes.text: Continue lowering the dumbbell until your elbows reach a 90 degree bend or until your upper arms begin to move backwards. Be sure to avoid making contact with the back of your head.
quotes.closest: Continue lowering the dumbbell until your elbows reach a 90 degree bend or until your upper arms begin to move backwards. Be sure to avoid making contact with the back of your head.

quotes.text: Attempt to keep your upper arms vertical to the floor throughout the exercise and your elbows shoulder-width apart.
quotes.closest: Attempt to keep your upper arms vertical to the floor throughout the exercise and your elbows shoulder-width apart.

quotes.text: Maintain your balance and avoid changing the position of your head, torso, upper arms, wrists and feet.
quotes.closest: Maintain your balance and avoid changing the position of your head, torso, upper arms, wrists and feet.

quotes.text: Depending on what type of resistance you use (dumbbell, kettlebell, band, etc.), sometimes the most difficult part is getting the weight into position. Use a weight that allows you to get to the starting position safely.
quotes.closest: Depending on what type of resistance you use (dumbbell, kettlebell, band, etc.), sometimes the most difficult part is getting the weight into position. Use a weight that allows you to get to the starting position safely.

quotes.text: If the weight is too heavy or you’re fatigued, you may be tempted to arch your back, which can increase the strain on your back and shoulder joints.
quotes.closest: If the weight is too heavy or you’re fatigued, you may be tempted to arch your back, which can increase the strain on your back and shoulder joints.

quotes.text: Keep the speed of movement relatively slow, and avoid momentum to focus on your form.
quotes.closest: Keep the speed of movement relatively slow, and avoid momentum to focus on your form.

quotes.text: Sit on a bench with back support or stand with feet shoulder-width apart, core engaged.
quotes.closest: Sit on a bench with back support or stand with feet shoulder-width apart, core engaged.

quotes.closest: Locking elbows at top

quotes.text: Spotting not typically required; assist by supporting elbows if needed for heavy sets.

quotes.text: Eccentric phase elicited less muscular activity than concentric in both exercises.
quotes.closest: Eccentric phase elicited less muscular activity than concentric in both exercises.

quotes.text: Concentric contraction presented the same pattern during OD (long and lateral heads) and LD (lateral head). Initial and middle intervals elicited higher muscle activity than final interval.
quotes.closest: Concentric contraction presented the same pattern during OD (long and lateral heads) and LD (lateral head). Initial and middle intervals elicited higher muscle activity than final interval.

quotes.text: The most common mechanism of injury was weights dropping on the person (65.5%). A large number of injuries occurred with free weights (90.4%).
quotes.closest: The most common mechanism of injury was weights dropping on the person (65.5%). A large number of injuries occurred with free weights (90.4%).

quotes.text: Triceps tendon ruptures (TTRs) are rare and often occur as a result of falling on an outstretched hand, forceful eccentric contraction, direct trauma to the elbow, or lifting against resistance.
quotes.closest: Triceps tendon ruptures (TTRs) are rare and often occur as a result of falling on an outstretched hand, forceful eccentric contraction, direct trauma to the elbow, or lifting against resistance.

quotes.text: When training at a specific RM load, it is recommended that 2-10% increase in load be applied when the individual can perform the current workload for one to two repetitions over the desired number.
